chapter: City bands, Johnny Dodds and the bag factory
title: Declining offers to play clarinet; Boston Penison and the guitar
summary: He kept the violin a long while, ducked musicians who wanted him, and praises a Baton Rouge guitarist who could imitate a mule.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: When you took up the clarinet, you didn't give up the violin then?

No, For a long while after that, I gave it up. And boys used to come here and get me, you know, to play with them, you know. But, uh, not Buddy P.T. That boy is dead. He was buried in the Gerard Cemetery. I forgot his name. But I played with several of them. The trumpet player, was it? Yeah, he was. A little light-skinned fella. I don't even forgot that boy's name.
Yeah, so many of them, yeah, I mixed up with. It wouldn't have been Chris Kelly. No, it wasn't Chris. I don't think he was light, was he? He was a little darker. It wasn't Chris. It wasn't Chris.
I didn't think who it would be then.

And so they wanted me to go away with them. I told them, no, I couldn't leave here. Sometimes I had to duck from them, you know. They come for me to play in different place with them, you know. It wouldn't have been Kid Rene. I believe that's the word, yeah, Kid? Kid Rene? That's the word. Because he was fairly light, I remember. Yeah, Kid Rene is right. I think it was fairly light. Oh, they want me to go with them, I... Sometime I duck them, they say, I'm coming at you tomorrow night. I say, okay. Yeah. They come, but I lied each year, you know. I checked the dude, he called, I would never answer.
They want you to play your clarinet? Play with them, yes.
Play my clarinet with them. Any instrument I'd put my hand on, I'd play guitar.

I could play a guitar. They had a fellow once, from where I was at, a place they called Grove State. He used to come there, they had an old bridge we used to settle on, you know, at night. He said, rap? I said, what? He said, you feel like playing something with me? I said, I don't care. I said, go get your guitar, and I'll go get my guitar, you know. How darn that fellow could play a guitar though. He, you know, make that guitar say most anything. The old mule coming at the, you know, at the gate and everything. His name was Boston Penison. He was from Baton Rouge. Yeah, you could, the old mule, you know, ha, ha, ha, all that bit. Just, just, just, just like that. That guitar almost all. And me and it. And so once some fellows came around there, they said, I said, boss, no, this boy is from here. I said, yeah, he lives right across the road. So, so he said, yeah. I said, oh, no, that boy ain't from here. I said, yes, he is. And play that good? I said, that's right. He plays with me all the time. Boss, Boston was a guitar player. You could just make it talk, you know, say most anything. And I don't see him sometime.
